leading_positions.synthesis: Four of eight members include B061 in their round-1 configuration, and all four name David R. Liu alone as laureate with near-identical citations on base editing as programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage. Aqvist makes it his whole prize; Brzezinski, Linke and Somfai pair it with a second part (see the paired entries below). What is shared is the single-leader attribution, the view that the chemistry (engineered deaminases, directed evolution of an adenine deaminase) is concrete, and the recognition that it follows the 2020 CRISPR prize. What is not shared is how much weight that proximity and the early clinical record deserve. Nishida and Kondo's concurrent cytidine-deaminase work is flagged as an open priority question by the supporters themselves, and Aili and Chabes list B061 only as an alternative.

Three members include B007 in their configuration, and all agree that Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated heterobifunctional degraders and that induced proximity turns ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis into a designable chemical reaction. They differ on who else is named and on the citation. Aili adds Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex design) under a PROTAC-centred citation; Chabes adds Handa (cereblon as the thalidomide target) and writes the molecular-glue mechanism into the citation; Brzezinski stops at Crews and Deshaies to leave room for a second part. Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim are named by nobody in a configuration. The group is also the one with the widest opening support (two first places, six rankings) but no member claims an approved degrader drug exists yet.

Brzezinski proposes a two-part prize: Crews and Deshaies for degraders, and Liu for base editing, presented as one achievement acting on proteins and one on nucleic acids. This is the only configuration that combines the two most widely supported ballots, but Brzezinski alone holds it, and it is reached by dropping Ciulli and Handa from B007.

The chair's own configuration pairs sequencing-by-synthesis (Balasubramanian and Klenerman; Rothberg excluded) with Liu for base editing, framed as reading and rewriting DNA. Only the chair prefers B001 in a configuration, although Aqvist lists it as a first alternative. The part is open to challenge on chemistry versus technology, on the 1980 DNA sequencing prize, and on the exclusion of Rothberg, Ju and Mayer.

Somfai pairs Buchwald and Hartwig for palladium-catalysed C-N coupling with Liu for base editing, one molecule-making part and one chemical-biology part. B022 is the only mature synthetic-methods case on the list with clean attribution, but it is seen as an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize and Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is an open precursor question.

Sparr prefers condensates alone (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen) as a general physical-chemical principle of multivalent phase separation. She herself notes limited opening support and contested in vivo relevance, and Aili and Aqvist both register maturity doubts. Pappu and Mittag fall outside the three seats.

Zou prefers molecular-sieve catalyst design (Corma, Davis, Zones) as a mature, large-scale, structurally proven field. Zou is the sole first-place voter and acknowledges that the theme is broad and hard to cite sharply, with Yu and Tsapatsis as possible alternative names.

areas_of_agreement: Every member's first choice is on the shortlist, and B007 or B061 appears in the configuration or alternatives of all eight members (Sparr and Zou list B007 as an alternative).
All four B061 supporters name Liu alone, so no member in a configuration disputes the single-laureate attribution; the dispute is whether Nishida and Kondo should also be credited.
All three B007 supporters credit Crews and Deshaies with the concept and first demonstration of heterobifunctional degraders.
Members who comment on degraders accept the mechanism as well confirmed and reproduced; reservations concern attribution and the lack of an approved degrader, not the science.
Members commenting on B007 or B061 (Aili, Chabes, Brzezinski, Aqvist, Linke, Somfai) treat clinical maturity as a live timing question: an approved degrader for B007, and long-term safety for B061.
Members who rank B061 (Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke, Somfai) describe the chemistry as concrete deaminase and nucleobase chemistry, and Aqvist explicitly distinguishes it from the 2020 nuclease prize.
scientific_disputes: Whether base editing is chemistry in its own right (engineered deaminase and directed evolution) or protein engineering around a known reaction and a continuation of the 2020 CRISPR prize (Somfai and Linke raise this against their own preference; Brzezinski and Aqvist also flag the 2020 proximity).

Whether sequencing-by-synthesis counts as chemistry or as biology and engineering, and whether the decisive step is the reversible-terminator chemistry or the optics and instrumentation (raised by Aili, Aqvist, Zou and the chair).

Whether the thalidomide/cereblon molecular-glue mechanism is part of the same principle as heterobifunctional PROTACs, as Chabes holds, or a separate mechanistic discovery that weakens a PROTAC citation, as Aili argues.
Whether C-N coupling is a new departure or an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize (raised by Somfai himself against his own preference).

Whether in vivo liquid-liquid phase separation is settled enough to be described as the functional organizing principle, or whether droplet-like behaviour may reflect overexpression and in vitro artefacts (Sparr, Aili).
attribution_disputes: B007: Crews and Deshaies are common to all three configurations, but the third seat is Ciulli (Aili), Handa (Chabes) or empty (Brzezinski); Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim are not named in any configuration.

B061: Liu alone versus a set that also credits Nishida and Kondo (concurrent cytidine-deaminase fusion) and the lead trainees Komor and Gaudelli; Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke and Somfai each flag this as unresolved.
B001: the chair's Balasubramanian and Klenerman pair omits Rothberg (454 pyrosequencing), Ju, Mayer and the cluster-amplification contributors; Aqvist doubts the Solexa and 454 split is obvious.
B022: Buchwald and Hartwig versus the prior claim of Kosugi's tin-amide coupling.
B034: Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen versus Pappu and Mittag within three seats.
B013: Corma, Davis and Zones versus Yu and Tsapatsis, and earlier work by Barrer, Breck and Flanigen that is not on the list.
maturity_disputes: B007: no approved degrader drug yet; Aili, Brzezinski, Chabes, Aqvist and Somfai all name this as a timing risk, while degraders in late-stage trials and independent reproduction are cited in favour.

B061: roughly a decade old with first patients treated, but long-term safety (off-target and bystander editing) is unsettled and the 2020 CRISPR prize is very recent; Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke and Somfai concede it may be early.
B001: more than fifteen years mature and broadly confirmed, but DNA sequencing was recognised in 1980 and the question is whether being overdue outweighs that.
B034: roughly fifteen years of reproduction in vitro, but in vivo functional relevance is contested.
B013 and B022: mature and widely deployed; the dispute is about novelty relative to earlier prizes and sharpness of the citation, not timing.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Brzezinski: work on proton and electron transfer in respiratory enzymes is close to B068 (Gray, Winkler) and bioenergetics topics; he flags this for any bioenergetics part and notes Xiaodong Zou is a Stockholm University colleague, relevant only to B013, with no recusal requested.

Zou: her electron-diffraction structure determination of zeolites and porous frameworks is scientifically close to B013 and she knows the community; she flags the proximity but has no stated tie to Corma, Davis or Zones.
Linke (chair): research on single-molecule nanoscale devices is closest to the nanopore ballot B044, held as an alternative only; no tie to any credited person.

Aili and Sparr: overlapping peptide and lipid assembly interests relevant to B034 and B049; Aili also notes that his postdoc mentors are not credited names; no direct tie to any shortlisted candidate.
Linke, Somfai and Sparr share a Lund University affiliation; Somfai and Sparr state this carries no stake in any candidate.
Aili, Aqvist, Chabes, Linke, Somfai and Sparr report no specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate beyond the above.
questions_for_round2: For B007, should the citation centre on PROTAC design (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli), include the cereblon molecular-glue mechanism (Crews, Deshaies, Handa), or stop at the concept (Crews, Deshaies)? Can any version be defended without Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim?

For B061, does the committee judge Nishida and Kondo's concurrent cytidine-deaminase work close enough in time and substance to change a Liu-alone attribution, and what is the minimum clinical evidence on safety and durability needed to call it mature?

How much weight should the 2020 CRISPR prize carry against B061, and how much should the absence of an approved degrader carry against B007? Should one of these be treated as the more mature of the two?

Is a two-part prize preferable to a single part, and if so which pairs are acceptable: B007 with B061 (Brzezinski), B001 with B061 (Linke) or B022 with B061 (Somfai)? Does any pair share a convincing common principle, or does the pairing exist only to bridge differing first choices?

For B001, is sequencing-by-synthesis decisive chemistry rather than biology and instrumentation, how does it differ in scope from the 1980 DNA sequencing prize, and how should credit be divided among Solexa and 454 lineages if the set is limited to three?

Does the committee regard B034 as mature enough, given contested in vivo relevance, and can three of Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag be named without an arbitrary cut? Similarly, can B013 be given a sharp citation naming three of Corma, Davis, Zones, Yu and Tsapatsis?

What would each member need to see (an additional name, a different citation, evidence of a first approval) in order to move a first-place vote from B013, B034, B022 or B001 toward a configuration that others on the committee already share?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows no majority configuration. B061 has the widest explicit backing (four of eight members include it, always with Liu alone), B007 has three, and each of B001, B022, B034 and B013 is a single member's preference. No two members hold the same full prize configuration. The two most supported ballots are each contested for timing and for a nearby earlier recognition or concurrent contributor, and attribution at B007 is the least settled of any leading position. Round 2 should settle the B007 citation and third name, the Nishida and Kondo question, and whether a two-part structure is acceptable. The chair participates as a member in this process and has tried to represent every position by what is written in the eight files.
